
Agents and people cite a rule by its ref (`WL-REQ-<n>`, `WL-RULE-<n>`) in code comments, commit messages, pull request bodies and docs, and never by a spec section number, because section numbers are derived from a spec's arrangement and change when it changes (WL-REQ-165). Three checks enforce it, and all three use one test: the text contains `<KEY>-SPEC-<n> §`, `<KEY>-SPEC-<n> sec-`, `#sec-`, or a `§` followed by digits that is not part of a rule ref.

1. **Context.** The context `lode-hook session-start` injects carries the instruction to cite rules by ref and never by spec section, and to read a section's rule ref with `lode show <doc>#sec-N`. It is injected in every checkout, inside or outside a Worklode worktree. `lode-hook subagent-start` injects the same text into each subagent the harness starts (WL-REQ-278). Both reach the harness in the shape WL-REQ-1725 names.
2. **Commit message.** The `commit-msg` git hook that `lode install` binds (WL-REQ-1721) rejects a message that fails the test, in every checkout of the repository. The rejection names each match and the rule ref it resolves to at the document's current version, resolved through the server under the hook timeout (WL-REQ-1722). When the server is unreachable the rejection names `lode show <doc>#sec-N` in place of the ref.
3. **Pull request.** `lode gate check` (WL-REQ-1549) applies the test to the pull request body and to the lines the diff adds, and fails naming each match the same way.

The `commit-msg` check runs in every checkout `lode install` manages. The gate check runs only in a repository with a `[gate]` table. The test skips text inside fenced code blocks, inline code spans and double quotes, and in URLs, since there a section marker is mentioned, not cited. A literal `#sec-N` placeholder in other prose trips the check; a rule ref followed by a section marker, such as `WL-REQ-165 §2`, passes.
